  PROBLEM: The assignment-prefix scans recognize `NAME=` but not Bash append assignments `NAME+=value`, so an assignment-prefixed `git push` is not recognized by the merged-PR guard.

  PROBLEM: `_ASSIGNMENT_RE` does not recognize Bash append assignments `NAME+=value`, so `_command_word_index` can mistake an assignment for the command and fail to classify the following `gh api` invocation.
  WHY: Reviewers report that this can trigger an unnecessary prompt for approved read-only calls or fail to prompt before a `gh api` write; severity disagreement: MAJOR and BLOCKER.

  PROBLEM: The `"secret" in lower` and `"credential" in lower` substring checks exclude ordinary paths whose components merely contain those words from isolated workspace snapshots.
  WHY: Agents can silently lose access to legitimate source files they are expected to read or edit; severity disagreement: MAJOR and NIT.

  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]

  WHY: The automated review editor cannot edit or fix that hook in its sandbox.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8662-8669 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict` returns success even when commit-and-push fails, and the resolved worktree is removed.
  WHY: The caller treats the invocation as successful and retries from scratch on later poll ticks, delaying failure detection and the CRITICAL alert until the lifetime cap; reviewers describe this as an intentional trade-off but flag its operational cost.

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py | lines 339-343 and line 621 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The command parsing regex matches simple variable assignments (NAME=) but does not match Bash append assignments (NAME+=).
  WHY: The merged-PR commit guard is bypassed for commands prefixed with NAME+=, returning exit code 0 (allow) instead of 2 (block) when pushing to a merged branch. This directly causes the CI failure in tests-hooks-and-orchestrator where tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py fails test_push_parser_guards_real_destination and test_template_copies_are_identical due to divergence from workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py | line 150: _ASSIGNMENT_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=") | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _ASSIGNMENT_RE does not match Bash append assignments (NAME+=value) in _command_word_index. When a command begins with an append assignment such as X+=1 gh api repos/owner/repo/issues, the assignment is not skipped as a prefix word.
  WHY: _command_word_index treats the assignment as the command word, preventing direct classification of the gh api call and triggering has_hidden_gh_api, which forces an interactive prompt (DECISION_ASK) even on approved read-only operations.
- scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py | lines 128-130 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The substring checks "secret" in lower and "credential" in lower in readonly_allowed() match any path part containing those substrings anywhere. This indiscriminately matches legitimate source code, tests, and documentation (e.g., src/auth/credential_service.py, tests/test_secrets.py, src/credentials.py).
  WHY: In read-only mode, legitimate repository files are omitted from the snapshot. In workspace mode, these files are not copied into the container, causing test suites importing them to fail with ModuleNotFoundError during agent execution, and any agent-created files matching the substring are ignored during copy_tree_state and never transferred back to the host repository.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py | line 40 and line 42 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The review editor workspace whitelist permits only gh_api_write_guard.py under .claude/hooks/. Line 42 rejects all other .claude/ files, preventing .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py from being snapshotted into or transferred out of the review editor workspace.
  WHY: The automated review editor cannot edit or fix .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py in the sandbox, blocking automated repair of the failing tests-hooks-and-orchestrator CI check run.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | lines 8665-8668 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict unconditionally returns 0 even when _integration_judge_commit_and_push fails due to intent fingerprint violations, remaining conflict markers, staging failures, or rejected pushes.
  WHY: The caller at line 10223 records a successful judge invocation, clears unresolved_ticks to 0, and reports that the judge resolved the conflict, even though the resolved worktree was destroyed and nothing was pushed to the integration branch. This delays error detection until subsequent poller cycles reach the cumulative lifetime cap.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py | lines 75-81 (READONLY_BAD_PARTS expansion) and lines 123-131 (the new "secret" / "credential" substring filter inside readonly_allowed) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN adds a substring filter `"secret" in lower or "credential" in lower` that is applied to every path part. Because Python's `in` matches anywhere in the part, legitimate source files whose names merely contain those substrings are silently excluded from both the read-only snapshot and the workspace copy. Real examples that would be removed from a consumer-repo agent's view: `secretary.md`, `secret_rotation.py`, `credential_helper.py`, `credential_provider.py`, `top_secret_utils.py`, `mycredentials.json`.
  WHY: A consumer repo that tracks a file like `src/credential_provider.py` or `scripts/secret_rotation.sh` will have that file absent from the agent's view. If a plan names it as a change site (very common in real codebases), the implement agent reports it as UNVERIFIED or fails to apply the change.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | lines 8662-8669 (invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict return contract) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN replaced the function's push-failure-propagating return with an unconditional `return 0`, with the call site also using `|| true` (`_integration_judge_commit_and_push "${judge_wt}" "${final_pr}" "${integration_branch}" "${default_branch}" || true; return 0`). A persistent push failure (branch protection, force-push protection, deleted branch, auth blip) now silently cycles through `heal_integration_branch_conflict` up to `INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX` (default 10) before a CRITICAL alert fires and the project is escalated to `ai:blocked`; the previous contract surfaced a failed publication on the first attempt.
  WHY: An operator observing the tracking issue sees repeated "judge exec completed" / "[integration-heal] Judge exec failed for integration conflict on PR #<N>" comments without an early CRITICAL alert. The alert only fires after `INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX` (default 10) consecutive dispatches, multiplying the time-to-alert for the first persistent failure by that factor.

  Expected change site: scripts/ai_engine.sh::claude_run (route through the credential-free, network-isolated container) and a new scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py broker (or equivalent) that holds the Anthropic credentials on the host.
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff has no scripts/ai_engine.s
